misconception_comparison.actual_revised_misconception: Replace the plus before cos(A-B) in the cosine-product identity by a minus, then substitute A+B=4alpha, A-B=-2beta and use cosine evenness; this yields (cos4alpha-cos2beta)/2.
misconception_comparison.evidence: The cosine-product identity is [cos(A+B)+cos(A-B)]/2. The stated wrong sign gives [cos(A+B)-cos(A-B)]/2. Substituting A=2alpha-beta and B=2alpha+beta yields A+B=4alpha, A-B=-2beta; cosine evenness gives exactly (cos4alpha-cos2beta)/2, the displayed distractor. The unchanged alpha=beta=0 counterexample gives original product 1 versus distractor 0. All expressions are defined for real alpha,beta. The revised named mistake now genuinely generates the false option; its independent truth and complete set remain unchanged.
